first_step_test: A low rounded head joins one long arched back and tapering tail. The underside remains open, so the learner can attach legs without erasing keeper contours.

source.notes: Six-panel direct graphite contact sheet; September 9 current lesson. No temporary scaffolding. Keep failed iterations private. First sheet rejected: six plates rather than planned seven and unclear far-front toes. Simplified new plan to six plates; fresh full-sheet generation required. Second sheet provides five early frames; finish recolored from saved step 5 to retain both hind-knee folds. Instruction order adjusted to observed early toe marks; no temporary guides.

frames.visible_job: Start at the small rounded snout on the left, rise gently into the neck, and sweep a broad arch over the back. Taper the line into a long tail on the right, turn around its tip, and stop beneath the tail. Leave the belly and leg area open.
frames.instruction: Start at the small rounded snout on the left, rise gently into the neck, and sweep a broad arch over the back. Taper the line into a long tail on the right, turn around its tip, and stop beneath the tail. Leave the belly and leg area open.

frames.visible_job: Below the shoulder, draw a short front leg with a flat foot. Add a wider hind leg below the rear body, join the belly between them, and add two narrower far legs behind the near pair. Stop their upper edges at the body. Add two short toe divisions on each near foot and one on the visible far hind foot; shade both far legs lightly.
frames.instruction: Below the shoulder, draw a short front leg with a flat foot. Add a wider hind leg below the rear body, join the belly between them, and add two narrower far legs behind the near pair. Stop their upper edges at the body. Add two short toe divisions on each near foot and one on the visible far hind foot; shade both far legs lightly.

frames.visible_job: Starting behind the neck, draw six pointed leaf-like plates attached along the back. Make the third plate tallest, then reduce their size toward the tail. Keep every plate above the back line and add a few light pencil strokes rising inside each one.
frames.instruction: Starting behind the neck, draw six pointed leaf-like plates attached along the back. Make the third plate tallest, then reduce their size toward the tail. Keep every plate above the back line and add a few light pencil strokes rising inside each one.

frames.step_name: Add the face and tail spikes
frames.visible_job: Place one small dark eye in the head, one nostril near the snout, and a short mouth line beneath it. Near the tail tip, draw four slim pointed spikes fanning away from their fixed attachments, with two above and two below the tail.
frames.instruction: Place one small dark eye in the head, one nostril near the snout, and a short mouth line beneath it. Near the tail tip, draw four slim pointed spikes fanning away from their fixed attachments, with two above and two below the tail.

frames.visible_job: Draw two small curved folds at the front edge of each near knee and a short crease across the front leg. Extend the established toe divisions into rounded toe tips without removing their lines. Sketch a narrow broken ground shadow beneath the feet and lightly hatch the underside.

final_step.visible_job: Add graphite value and restrained olive and ochre within the established dinosaur contours.
final_step.instruction: Shade the underside and far legs with soft graphite. Layer muted olive lightly across the body and warm ochre inside the six plates, leaving the upper back pale. Deepen the existing ground shadow and keep the paper grain visible without adding new outlines.
adds: graphite value and restrained olive and ochre color

visual_review.first_step_observation: The first crop contains only one long connected head-back-tail silhouette and an open underside. The small snout notch is part of that contour, not a separate guide. A beginner can copy the low head and arch before attaching legs.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: Read all six final instructions against the five saved pairs, then checked the repaired final pair and assembled sequence again. Early toe marks are taught with legs; six plates, four tail spikes, knee folds and ground are present before color. There are no temporary guides or unexplained erased keeper lines.
